newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH 1996 BUDGET ENDS WITH CZK 419MLN SURPLUS - CTK.
newsitem.headline: CZECH 1996 BUDGET ENDS WITH CZK 419MLN SURPLUS - CTK.

text.p: The Czech 1996 state budget showed a surplus of 419 million crowns according to preliminary results of the Finance Ministry, the local CTK news agency reported on Thursday, quoting the ministry's chief of staff.
It quoted Hynek Rasocha as saying that 1996 revenue totalled 482.797 billion crowns while expenditure was 482.378 billion crowns. The final result is expected in mid-January.
Ministry officials were not immediately available for further comment.
The result would be a surprise after the government took steps in December to freeze selective spending in an effort to keep an expected budget deficit below 1.2 billion crowns.

Government officials said in December that the forecast deficit, without the spending freezes and some early payments on credit due from non-budget government agencies, could have been more than five billion crowns, because of lower than expected revenue.

In the autumn the government made across the board spending cuts in order to avoid a forecast 9.3 billion crown shortfall, caused by high-than-expected spending, slow repayments on credits to Russia, and lower than expected tax revenue.
The 1996 budget was originally approved as a balanced budget totalling 497 billion crowns, but the autumn spending cuts knocked the forecast expenditure down to 491 billion crowns.
The government of Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus has managed four straight budgets ending with in a surplus, and parliament approved a fifth straight balanced budget plan in December.
